In one version of this song, the singer notes that a certain institution "don't mean shit if you've got the right friends" and claims to be "the new folk hero of the Ku Klux Klan"; that version was rewritten to reference the Moscone-Milk assassinations by the Dead Kennedys. It was originally written by Sonny Curtis and recorded by the post-Buddy-Holly Crickets, though the first charting version was recorded by the Bobby Fuller Four. In the original version of this song, the singer twice admits "guess my race is run" and begins the song with the line "Breakin' rocks in the hot sun". Identify this song most famously covered by The Clash, whose singer ultimately suffers the consequences of "robbin' people with a six-gun".

One of this film's protagonists is first introduced in a drunken sleep with his nose pressed against the wall, causing his acquaintance to drag him to a bathtub and stick his face in a sinkful of ice to try to wake him. The actor who played this movie's antagonist claimed that a handball injury allowed him to affect his character's limp. This film's antagonist is an "Irishman who doesn't drink, doesn't smoke, and doesn't chase dames," who is cheated at cards on a train but cannot pay up because the cheaters had previously stolen his wallet. Its plot revolves around a half-million-dollar bet on "Lucky Dan" placed by Doyle Lonnegan, played by Robert Shaw. Marvin Hamlisch adapted works like "Solace," "The Easy Winners," and "The Entertainer" for this film, whose soundtrack repopularized Scott Joplin. Name this 1973 George Roy Hill film in which Paul Newman and Robert Redford put on the title con.

A spin-off of this video game series featured the heroic title knight battling Evil Ed. Besides The Adventures of Lomax, this series features an entry which separated the title characters into groups like "Space," "Egyptian," and "Highland" and allowed for the learning of permanent, continuous, and temporary skills. This series was created by a team working for Psygnosis who was inspired after creating an endlessly moving pixel character for the game Walker. One entry in this series featured 100 new levels and was titled Oh No! More [this series], while the official second entry was subtitled The Tribes. In this series, the player assigns such skills as "Diggers," "Floaters," and "Bombers," and also has the option to "nuke" any remaining title characters in order to end the level. Name this game series where you try to save the title little guys from committing mass suicide.

This character once became Secretary of Defense under the name "Dell Rusk." He was responsible for funding the right-wing group the Watchdogs and enjoyed playing Chopin's funeral march as he killed his victims. This man's most frequent aide is Brock Rumlow, who killed Diamondback's brother. His identity was also used by the Communist Albert Malik, who ordered the murder of Peter Parker's parents. This character kills people with the "Dust of Death," has a daughter named Sin, and frequently used clone bodies prepared by Dr. Arnim Zola. A 2011 film saw Hugo Weaving play this character, who was deformed by Dr. Erskine's super soldier serum and broke from the Nazis to found HYDRA. Name this crimson headed villain who usually opposes Captain America.

This substance is the key ingredient found in ajo blanco that distinguishes it from gazpacho, another cold soup. They are fried and ground up with sesame and anise seeds when making sellou or sfouf. According to Pausanias, the castrated penis of the hermaphrodite Agdistis grew into this kind of tree, and when one of these was placed in the bosom of the nymph Nana, she gave birth to Attis. This substance is the typical garnish for pasanda curries and was traditionally soaked in water overnight to make korma. Their scent reminds Dr. Juvenal Urbino of the fate of unrequited love in Love in the Time of Cholera, and they are ground into a flour to make frangipane, French macarons, amaretti, and marzipan. Their bitter variety contains small quantities of hydrogen cyanide. Name this drupe found in a certain candy bar recommended for those "times you feel like a nut", rather than a Mounds.

One character in this movie is enraged when the band plays "Pop Goes the Weasel" instead of a traditional tune he requests. During one scene in this film, a character jokes that "the family had a lot of buffers," while another scene has a discussion of plotters against the Roman Emperor being allowed to slit their wrists. The ending has the protagonist called stupid for joining the Marines on his father's birthday. After the protagonist of this film tells someone "I know it was youyou broke my heart," that character is later slain while reciting the Hail Mary on Lake Tahoe. It ends after the protagonist has ordered the deaths of Hyman Roth and his own brother, Fredo, contrasting him with the beloved image of his Robert De Niro played father as seen in various flashbacks. Name this 1974 movie which continues the story of Michael Corleone.

It's not New Year's, but as part of a "game" for this day, Gawain beheaded the Green Knight. On this day, The Witch's Curse is performed by Jo and her sisters; earlier on this day, the Marches donated their breakfasts to the Hummels. A little girl wishes for this day to recur in a William Dean Howells short story about "[it] Every Day." A character spends this holiday with a crutched boy who declares, "God Bless Us, Everyone One!" On the evening prior, that character was visited by three Ghosts and Jacob Marley. Identify this holiday which provokes "Bah, humbug!" comments from Ebenezer Scrooge in a Dickens novella about its namesake Carol.

SV Dynamo served as a center for mandatory doping of athletes in this country. An agency in this country attempted to "biodegrade" its opponents by covertly rearranging objects and tapping phones. The Practika camera and the Trabant automobile were made in this country. The SED was a party formed by the merger of the KPD and the SPD in this country and was led by Walter Ulbricht. Good relations with it were promoted by Willy Brandt. Its secret police was called the Stasi. In an attempt to stop brain drain from it, a giant wall was built in its capital, Berlin. Name this country that was led by Ernst Hoenecker and reunited in 1990 with its western counterpart.

Desserts from this country include the caramel-custard-and-meringue "floating island," which is also called "eggs in snow." Savory dishes from this country are often based on a mixture of chopped celery, onions, and carrots. A chef from this country put raspberry sauce on vanilla ice cream and peaches and named it after soprano Nellie Melba. Many sauces from it are based on flour cooked in butter, a roux ["roo"]. A chef from this country codified its five "mother sauces," including Béchamel and Hollandaise. Dishes from this country include thin filled pancakes which are set on fire, or flambéed, called Crêpe Suzette. Name this European birthplace of Brie and croissants.

This chess piece is the third moved by black in the Nimzo-Indian Defence. A pawn in front of this piece is the first piece moved by black in the Caro-Kann Defence; that pawn is also the first piece moved by White in the English Opening. The placement of one of these pieces is the difference between the Italian Game and the Ruy ["roy"] Lopez. They are placed on the second rank and surrounded by pawns in a "fianchetto." Its pawn is proffered in the Queen's Gambit and is first piece moved by Black in the Sicilian Defence. They are "bad" when blocked by pawns of their own color. Like knights, they are "worth" three points. Name these chess pieces that start next to the King and Queen and can only move diagonally.
